I am 54 years old and have farmed these lands in Quzhou for 35 years. My father taught me, and now I know every mu. With 64 mu and only part of my household labor available — my children work in the city — I cannot take too many risks or manage overly complex intercropping. Cotton is my backbone; it always has been. This year I will plant 34 mu of cotton with improved seeds, not the newest hybrids because I know what works. I will apply fertilizer generously but not wastefully — about 20 kg nitrogen per mu plus some phosphorus and potassium — and irrigate four times from my well. The well water is precious, so cotton gets priority. I will spray five times because bollworms and aphids never rest. For food security, I keep 15 mu of winter wheat with improved seed; I rotary till in autumn, irrigate three times, and expect about 520 kg per mu. Immediately after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize on that same 15 mu using no-tillage — there is no time to plough, and the machine can sow directly into stubble. Maize needs less water, so two well irrigations plus summer rain should give me 600 kg per mu. Stevia brings good cash income — the company sends trucks to our village — so I devote 15 mu to it. Stevia needs moderate fertilizer, three irrigations, and two pesticide sprays. I expect about 200 kg of dry leaves per mu. Keeping crops in separate blocks is easier for my wife and me to manage without help during peak seasons.
